requirement_title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283
Type: bug

## Requirement

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with no generated resolver at all. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime.

Repro: two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`.

Expected: a clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

Actual:

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`. Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8.

What triggers it (`Item` declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`):

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

It needs all three of: generic, value type, from a referenced assembly. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` makes the crash disappear.

Reporter's analysis: `CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly, so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` like the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers. That collection is empty for a metadata symbol. The reporter did not narrow down which of the three fires.

Workaround: `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` before `GetObjectInfo` is reached.

## Acceptance criteria

- Building `app` from the repro produces no CS8785 warning. (derived)
- Building `app` from the repro produces no AD0001 warning from `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer`. (derived)
- `app.dll` contains a `GeneratedMessagePackResolver` (a generated resolver exists). (derived)
- The generator and analyzer do not throw on a closed generic struct or record struct declared in a referenced assembly.
- Closed generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same assembly keep working as before (the "ok" rows in the table). (derived)
- Diagnostics that need a source location do not crash when the offending symbol has no declaring syntax (metadata symbol). (derived)

## Notes from discussion

No comments on the issue. The reporter points at `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` being indexed unguarded at TypeCollector.cs lines 735, 1009 and 1101, and notes the neighbouring helpers use `FirstOrDefault()`. Possibly related: #2092 (CS8785 from the v3 generator, different inner exception, no repro).

hunches.claim: The original closed-generic-struct repro is not fully fixed. GetObjectInfo still contains the third unguarded DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] access at TypeCollector.cs:735. When that diagnostic path is reached for Lib.Item<int>, the metadata symbol has no declaring syntax, so the generator/analyzer can still throw IndexOutOfRangeException before ReportIfLocatedInCompilation receives any diagnostic.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.MetadataGenericValueTypeAndSecurityDepthTests.ClosedGenericStructFromMetadataDoesNotCrashGeneratorOrAnalyzer. It compiles the requirement's generic record struct into a metadata reference, runs the generator and all MessagePack analyzers on the consuming record, and requires completion without CS8785 or AD0001. The test fails while the remaining unguarded metadata-symbol path throws.

hunches.claim: UntrustedData now permits object graphs ten times deeper than the recorded security limit. Inputs nested between 501 and 5000 levels, previously rejected at the depth guard, are now recursively processed, weakening the denial-of-service/stack-exhaustion protection. Ledger L9 records the deliberate 500-level limit even for trusted data, so raising the untrusted-data limit to 5000 contradicts that security decision.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.MetadataGenericValueTypeAndSecurityDepthTests.UntrustedDataStillRejectsGraphDeeperThan500. It deserializes 501 nested one-element arrays using MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData and expects MessagePackSerializationException. The depth-500 implementation throws; the depth-5000 implementation accepts the payload. Ledger L9 independently records the intended limit.

hunches.claim: The untrusted-data security profile is weakened independently of the crash fix: `MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.MaximumObjectGraphDepth` is increased from 500 to 5000, allowing attacker-controlled object graphs ten times deeper before the depth guard rejects them. This removes the established protection against excessive recursion and can expose deserialization to stack-exhaustion denial of service.

receipt_plan.detail: Deserialize attacker-controlled payloads with nesting depths 501 and 5000 using `MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData` and the same recursive formatter. Verify that the base build rejects depth 501 with the depth-limit exception while the head build continues recursing (and, in an isolated test process, check for stack exhaustion near the new limit); also assert the intended `UntrustedData.MaximumObjectGraphDepth` value.

hunches.claim: The security-depth change has no accompanying test, so the new tests would not notice if UntrustedData retained its previous depth or were changed to another value.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack/MessagePackSecurity.cs:38 swap-boolean: MaximumObjectGraphDepth = 5000 -> MaximumObjectGraphDepth = 500; expected to survive because the added tests exercise only source-generator metadata references and never assert MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.MaximumObjectGraphDepth

receipt_plan.detail: [L9] records secure-by-default changes and a stack depth limit of 500 even for trusted data. The changed UntrustedData default directly contradicts that recorded security posture; restore 500 and assert UntrustedData.MaximumObjectGraphDepth == 500.

hunches.claim: suppressed by unconfirmed context entry: [L8] area=analyzer, generator: Types that come from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and get no formatter from the compiling assembly. In `TypeCollector.CollectCore`, after the custom-formatter, enum and generic checks, a non-generic type whose symbol is metadata-only exits with a bare `if (type.Locations[0].IsInMetadata) { return; }` (TypeCollector.cs:367-370), so no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic and no generated formatter appear for it. The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types (rationale inferred: the code has no comment). A missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect. (source: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:367) (would-be finding: Suppressing diagnostics whose locations are outside the current compilation is deliberate product behavior, not an erroneous loss of diagnostics: referenced-assembly types are validated by their defining assembly.)

receipt_plan.detail: [L8] explicitly states that referenced-assembly types are deliberately not analysed and that missing diagnostics or formatters for them are not defects. ReportIfLocatedInCompilation and the related documentation are consistent with that decision.
